Iowa Conference champion | bowl = [[Stagg Bowl]] | bowl_result = W 10–8 vs. {{cfb link|year=1974|team=Ithaca Bombers|title=Ithaca}} }} {{1974 Iowa Conference football standings}} The '''1974 Central Dutch football team''' was an [[American football]] team that represented [[Central College (Iowa)|Central College]] as a member of the [[American Rivers Conference|Iowa Conference]] during the [[1974 NCAA Division III football season]]. In their 11th season under head coach [[Ron Schipper]], the Dutch compiled an 11–0 record and won both the Iowa Conference championship and the NCAA Division III national championship.{{cite web|title=1974 Football Schedule|publisher=Central College|accessdate=October 24, 2021|url=https://athletics.central.edu/sports/football/schedule/1974}}{{cite web|title=2019 Central College Media Guide|publisher=Central College|year=2019|accessdate=October 25, 2021|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/sidearm.sites/central.sidearmsports.com/documents/2019/8/21/2019_Football_Media_Guide.pdf}} The team participated in the second annual NCAA Division III playoff, defeating {{cfb link|year=1974|team=Evansville Purple Aces|title=Evansville}} (17–16) in the semifinal and {{cfb link|year=1974|team=Ithaca Bombers|title=Ithaca}} (10–8) in the [[Amos Alonzo Stagg Bowl]] championship game. Linebacker Al Dorenkamp led a defense that allowed an average of only 6.9 points per game and was selected as the most valuable player in the IIAC.2019 Media Guide, pp. 56, 99. Eight Central players received first-team honors on the All-IIAC team: Dorenkamp; offensive linemen Don Knock and Dan Wright; wide receiver Randy Busscher; running back Mike Hodges; quarterback Gary Cutler; defensive lineman Ron Merema; and defensive back Cliff Marlow.2019 Media Guide, p. 56. Quarterback Cutler completed 69 of 126 passes for 1,236 yards and 16 touchdowns.2019 Media Guide, p. 33. His 1974 pass efficiency rating of 174.3 remains a single-season school record (minimum 100 attempts). Receiver Busscher set a single-game school record with 259 receiving yards in the victory over {{cfb link|year=1974|team=Ferris State Bulldogs|title=Ferris State}}.2019 cMedia Guide, p. 43. Coach Schipper was honored as the 1974 IIAC Coach of the Year. He was inducted in the [[College Football Hall of Fame]] in 2000.{{cite web|title=Ron Schipper|publisher=National Football Foundation|accessdate=October 25,
